sections.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars
sections.abstract: Using Hipparcos and Gaia astrometry for 63,254 stars, the authors infer that the brown-dwarf companion deficit is centered near a 1.8% companion-to-star mass ratio across host masses, rather than at a fixed companion mass.
sections.claimed_result: The authors estimate the desert minimum at q = 1.76 (+0.26/-0.19)%, with opposite metallicity trends below and above it, consistent with distinct formation channels.
sections.evidence_type: observational; hierarchical population analysis of Hipparcos and Gaia DR2/DR3 astrometry, with Gaia DR3 metallicities for a subset
sections.unique_caveat: Inference is limited to modeled 3–94-year orbits and nonuniform astrometric sensitivity; Gaia DR4 should sharpen some constraints, while longer periods still benefit from Hipparcos.

sections.title: Search for a Dispersion Measure Excess Toward Nearby Galaxy Halos Using Fast Radio Bursts from the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog
sections.abstract: A stack of 1,748 localized CHIME/FRB sources yields a tentative dispersion-measure excess toward nearby galaxy halos, which the authors use to constrain circumgalactic electron density.
sections.claimed_result: For halos within 50 Mpc, the authors find a mean DM excess of 119 ± 44 pc cm⁻³ (p = 0.0053, about 2.6σ); the impact-parameter trend out to 150 Mpc is also about 2.6σ and is described as tentative.
sections.evidence_type: observational; stacking and cross-correlation analysis of the Second CHIME/FRB Baseband Catalog and nearby-galaxy samples
sections.unique_caveat: The signal is modest; host-galaxy FRBs can bias the smallest-impact-parameter bins, and finite FRB localization blurs the inferred halo profile.

sections.title: AGN Feedback Turbulence in Cool-core Clusters: Evidence from XRISM
sections.abstract: XRISM velocity measurements and tailored simulations suggest that AGN-driven turbulence dominates the core of A1795, while merger-driven motions dominate in A2029, consistent with an evolutionary picture for cool-core clusters.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer feedback-dominated velocity dispersion in A1795's core, potentially supplying turbulent heating comparable to radiative cooling, but only an upper limit on AGN feedback in A2029, where merger motions dominate.
sections.evidence_type: observational; XRISM cluster velocity profiles interpreted with turbulent and tailored merger simulations
sections.unique_caveat: Separating feedback from merger motions depends on simplified turbulence prescriptions and uncertain merger geometry; the A2029 feedback estimate is explicitly only an upper limit.

sections.title: First demonstration of long-distance electron drift in liquid xenon with the Xenoscope time projection chamber
sections.abstract: The Xenoscope chamber demonstrates electron drift over 2.6 m in liquid xenon and measures drift velocities at two electric-field strengths, providing a benchmark for future large xenon detectors.
sections.claimed_result: Using cosmic-muon ionization and external muon timing, the authors measure drift velocities of 1.320 ± 0.006 mm/μs at 80.92 ± 0.36 V/cm and 1.436 ± 0.001 mm/μs at 96.00 ± 0.42 V/cm over 2.6 m.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; dual-phase liquid-xenon Xenoscope time-projection chamber with cosmic-muon signals and external muon tagging
sections.unique_caveat: This demonstrates long drift and charge readout in a prototype, not the performance of a full-scale next-generation observatory under all operating conditions.

sections.title: Tetragonal-to-orthorhombic distortion in CeRh$_{2}$As$_{2}$
sections.abstract: Directional thermal-expansion measurements on CeRh₂As₂ show a very small orthorhombic distortion below its phase-I ordering temperature, constraining possible order parameters in this superconducting material.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find broken fourfold in-plane symmetry below T₀ ≈ 0.46 K and argue that this constrains phase-I order and may disfavor a multicomponent superconducting order parameter developing within phase I.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; longitudinal thermal-expansion measurements along four in-plane crystallographic directions on a single crystal
sections.unique_caveat: The structural distortion is extremely small and the phase-I order parameter remains undetermined; implications for superconducting symmetry are conditional.

sections.title: Forward modeling linear variable filter data: High resolution PAH and Paschen-$\alpha$ maps from SPHEREx
sections.abstract: The authors forward-model SPHEREx linear-variable-filter observations to make higher-resolution PAH and Paschen-α emission maps with reduced striping artifacts in selected Galactic and nearby-galaxy fields.
sections.claimed_result: The authors produce 3.3-μm and 3.4-μm maps for fields including M31, M33, the Rosette Nebula, and Corona Australis, reporting a 3.3-μm sensitivity as low as 2.7 × 10⁻⁸ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² sr⁻¹ in the demonstrated fields.
sections.evidence_type: computational; forward modeling of SPHEREx linear-variable-filter data, with pixel-level data handling, stellar masking, and conditional Gaussian-process infill
sections.unique_caveat: The paper demonstrates selected fields rather than a completed all-sky PAH map; WISE-like sensitivity from a two-year survey extension is a forecast dependent on a modified scan strategy.
